done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test or finding, or the change grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it

findings.body: Raise: Not done. For a client configured with `tools = "claude"` or `tools = "codex"`, the question omits the required switch choice, and `forge close --resolve switch` rejects it at close.py:99. The owner therefore cannot choose the other tool for that item.
findings.title: Not done: single-tool clients cannot choose the other tool

findings.body: Raise: Functional. Test names are recognized only on lines containing `FAILED` and a `::` identifier. When a supported Jest or Vitest client reports failures without that format, every failure becomes the same check label. Two fix rounds that leave different failing tests under `tests` are then treated as the same stuck problem, so Forge stops the item before the stated condition is met.
findings.title: Different failing tests in one check can falsely stop an item

findings.body: Raise: Test. The named proof covers a repeated synthetic failing test, but no command-level test covers a repeated review finding or the `same`, `narrow`, and `split` choices. Its switch check reaches `forge work` only to assert Codex's setup refusal; `worker.ready` rejects that call before a Codex turn starts. The size-limit proof likewise stops at the question. The required next-round behavior therefore has no end-to-end proof.
findings.title: Not done: test repeated findings and the worker round after a choice

why: When a worker can't fix a problem or keeps making the change bigger, Forge sends it back round after round and nobody is told
